title: Who needs a pesticide training certificate under the EU Sustainable Use Directive?
description: Directive 2009/128/EC Article 5 and Annex I: certificates for professional users, distributors and advisors, the 13 training subjects and the sales rules.
shortAnswer: Directive 2009/128/EC, the Sustainable Use Directive, requires every EU Member State to give professional users, distributors and advisors of plant protection products access to initial and additional training, and to run certification systems proving sufficient knowledge of the 13 subjects in Annex I. Certification systems had to exist by 14 December 2013. Sales of professional products are restricted to certificate holders, and distributors must employ certified staff available at the point of sale.
keyTakeaways: The directive applies to pesticides that are plant protection products (Article 2(1)); it covers three roles defined in Article 3: professional users, distributors and advisors.
Article 5(1) requires access to initial and additional training by bodies designated by the competent authorities; Article 5(2) required certification systems by 14 December 2013.
Annex I lists 13 training subjects, from legislation and counterfeit products to integrated pest management, sprayer calibration, emergency action and record keeping.

Article 6 requires distributors to have sufficient certified staff available at the time of sale and restricts sales of professional products to certificate holders, with both measures due by 14 December 2015.
The directive leaves certificate validity, renewal intervals and course hours to Member States, so national rules decide when a certificate must be renewed.
jurisdiction: European Union (all Member States; directive transposed into national law)
regulator: European Commission (Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety) under Directive 2009/128/EC, with competent authorities designated by each Member State for certification
appliesTo: Professional users of plant protection products, including operators, technicians, employers and self-employed people in farming and other sectors
Distributors, including wholesalers, retailers, vendors and suppliers
Advisors on pest management and safe pesticide use, including commercial agents and public advisory services

sections.heading: Who must be trained and certified under Directive 2009/128/EC?

blocks.text: Three groups must have access to training and must be able to obtain a certificate: professional users, distributors and advisors. [Directive 2009/128/EC](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32009L0128) of 21 October 2009 establishing a framework for Community action to achieve the sustainable use of pesticides entered into force on 25 November 2009, and Member States had to transpose it by 14 December 2011.

items: **Professional user:** "any person who uses pesticides in the course of their professional activities, including operators, technicians, employers and self-employed people, both in the farming and other sectors". That reaches groundskeepers, rail and road verge contractors and amenity teams as well as farmers.
**Distributor:** any natural or legal person who makes a pesticide available on the market, including wholesalers, retailers, vendors and suppliers.

**Advisor:** any person who has acquired adequate knowledge and advises on pest management and the safe use of pesticides in a professional capacity or commercial service, including private self-employed and public advisory services, commercial agents, food producers and retailers where applicable.

blocks.text: Although Article 3(10) defines "pesticide" to include biocidal products, Article 2(1) limits the directive's scope to pesticides that are plant protection products as defined in Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. Biocide user training, where it exists, comes from other rules.

Article 5 requires training and certification, and Article 6 links certification to the sale of products. Article 5(1) states that Member States "shall ensure that all professional users, distributors and advisors have access to appropriate training by bodies designated by the competent authorities", consisting of "both initial and additional training to acquire and update knowledge as appropriate".

items: **Role based design (Article 5(1)):** training must give each group sufficient knowledge of the Annex I subjects, taking account of their different roles and responsibilities. A distributor course and a sprayer operator course are not expected to be identical.

**Certification systems (Article 5(2)):** by 14 December 2013, Member States had to establish certification systems and designate competent authorities. Certificates must at least prove sufficient knowledge of Annex I, acquired through training or by other means.
**Granting, renewal and withdrawal (Article 5(2)):** each certification system must include requirements and procedures for all three. The directive does not fix a validity period.

**Distributor staffing (Article 6(1)):** distributors must have sufficient staff holding a certificate, available at the time of sale to give customers information on use, health and environmental risks, and safety instructions.

**Restricted sales (Article 6(2)):** Member States must restrict sales of pesticides authorized for professional use to persons holding a certificate. The measures in Article 6(1) and (2) had to be in place by 14 December 2015.
**Aerial spraying (Article 9):** where aerial spraying is permitted by derogation, the operator carrying it out must hold a certificate under Article 5(2).

blocks.text: Micro distributors selling only products for non-professional use may be exempted from the staffing rule if they do not sell formulations classified as toxic, very toxic, carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic for reproduction (Article 6(1)).

sections.heading: Which 13 subjects does Annex I require?

blocks.text: Annex I lists 13 training subjects, and every certificate must evidence sufficient knowledge of them. The list below summarizes each one and suggests an assessable outcome; the outcomes are an original illustration, not text from the directive.

blocks.text: Annex I has not been amended since 2009. Regulation (EU) 2019/1243 replaced Article 5(3) so that the Commission may now amend Annex I by delegated act to take account of scientific and technical progress. Any future change to the subject list would come that way.

sections.heading: Which other parts of the directive depend on trained staff?

blocks.text: Several other obligations assume that certified users know how to apply them. Training content should cover them even though they sit outside Article 5.

items: **Equipment inspection (Article 8):** application equipment in professional use must be inspected at intervals not exceeding three years after 2020, and Annex I item 9 requires users to know the objectives of those technical checks.

**Integrated pest management (Article 14):** Member States had to describe in their National Action Plans how the general IPM principles in Annex III would be implemented by all professional users by 1 January 2014. Annex I items 4 and 5 are the training counterpart.

**National Action Plans (Article 4):** plans set targets and measures, including worker protection, and must be reviewed at least every five years. Training requirements and renewal intervals are often found in these plans and the transposing law.

blocks.title: Where to find renewal rules
blocks.text: Because the directive sets no certificate validity period or minimum course length, the renewal interval, the number of hours and any continuing education credits are national. An organization operating in several Member States needs a country by country register of certificate types and renewal dates.

sections.heading: Is the Sustainable Use Directive changing?

blocks.text: As at November 2026, Directive 2009/128/EC remains in force, and the current consolidated version on EUR-Lex dates from 26 July 2019. The amendments since adoption concern the abolition of Article 22, a replacement of Annex IV by Directive (EU) 2019/782, and procedural changes by Regulation (EU) 2019/1243, including the new basis for amending Annex I.

None of those amendments changed the training and certification duties in Articles 5 and 6 or the Annex I subjects. Teams should still monitor national transposing law, where renewal periods and course formats are set, using a process like the one in [how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats each Annex I item as a defined knowledge point with role specific outcomes for users, distributors and advisors, so one framework can produce three differentiated courses that still trace back to the same 13 subjects. Assessment items are attached to each point, which makes it straightforward to show a certification body that every subject is covered for every role.

faqs.q: How long is an EU pesticide user certificate valid?
faqs.a: Directive 2009/128/EC does not set a validity period. Article 5(2) only requires each certification system to include requirements and procedures for granting, renewing and withdrawing certificates. The validity period, renewal training and any continuing education are set in each Member State's transposing law or National Action Plan.

faqs.q: Does the directive apply to biocide users such as pest control technicians?
faqs.a: Not directly. Article 2(1) limits the directive to pesticides that are plant protection products under Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009, even though the Article 3 definition of pesticide also mentions biocidal products. Training for biocide users, where required, comes from biocide rules or national law.

faqs.q: Can a certificate be obtained without attending a course?
faqs.a: Article 5(2) allows certificates to evidence sufficient knowledge of the Annex I subjects acquired either by undergoing training or by other means. Whether a Member State accepts examination only routes or prior qualifications is a national decision, so the answer differs between countries.

faqs.q: Do retail shop staff selling garden products need a certificate?
faqs.a: Distributors must have sufficient certified staff available at the time of sale under Article 6(1), but micro distributors selling only products for non-professional use may be exempted if they do not sell formulations classified as toxic, very toxic, carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic for reproduction. Distributors selling to non-professionals must still give general risk information under Article 6(3).
